questions.question: A running copy of a Docker image is called a _____.
questions.explanation: The image is the recipe; the container is the dish cooked from it, actually running.

questions.question: What is a Docker image?
options: A program that is currently running
A read-only package with a program and everything it needs
A virtual machine with Windows inside
A backup copy of your database data
questions.explanation: An image is a read-only template used to start containers. A is tempting, but the running thing is the container, not the image.

questions.question: Is it true that you can start several containers from the same image?
questions.explanation: Like cooking one recipe many times, each container is a separate running copy of the same image.

questions.question: In an image name like postgres:17, the part after the colon is called the _____.
questions.explanation: The tag picks the version, so everyone who uses the same tag gets the same Postgres major version.

questions.question: Why run a database in a container instead of installing it directly on Windows?
questions.answer: Because the same image gives exactly the same version and settings on your PC, in CI and in production, and nothing gets installed on Windows itself.
questions.explanation: Delete the container and your system is clean again, and every machine runs the identical database version.

questions.question: Is it true that Docker Desktop runs Linux containers directly on the Windows kernel?
questions.explanation: Linux containers need a Linux kernel. Docker Desktop runs them inside a small Linux virtual machine provided by WSL 2.

questions.question: Why can Docker Desktop fail with "virtualization isn't enabled"?
options: You are not logged in to Docker Hub
The image tag does not exist
WSL 2 runs a virtual machine, which needs hardware virtualization turned on
Port 5432 is already used by another program
questions.explanation: WSL 2 is a real virtual machine, so the CPU's virtualization and the Windows virtual machine feature must be on. The other problems give different errors, after Docker has started.

questions.question: In a port mapping like 8080:80, the first number is the port on your _____.
questions.explanation: The format is "host port : container port": traffic to port 8080 on your PC goes to port 80 inside the container.

questions.question: Is it true that data written inside a container survives when the container is deleted, even without a volume?
questions.explanation: Without a volume, the data lives in the container and is deleted with it. A volume stores it outside, so a new container finds it again.

questions.question: Why might the official Postgres image ignore your setup script the second time the database starts?
questions.answer: Because init scripts run only when the data volume is empty. On later starts the database already exists, so the scripts are skipped.
questions.explanation: To rerun the init scripts you must delete the volume so the database starts from scratch.

questions.question: What does a healthcheck tell Docker?
options: Whether the image has finished downloading
How much memory the container uses
Whether the program inside is actually ready to work
questions.explanation: A healthcheck repeats a small test (like pg_isready) until it passes. A container can be "running" before the program inside is ready, which is why A or a simple "started" is not enough.

questions.question: Why wait for the database to be healthy before running the tests?
questions.answer: Because the database needs a few seconds to start after the container starts, and tests run too early would fail to connect.
questions.explanation: --wait or a healthcheck in CI holds the tests back until the database is ready.

questions.question: Which command runs a program inside a container that is already running?
questions.explanation: exec runs a command in a running container, for example psql. B is tempting, but up starts containers; it does not run extra programs inside them.

questions.question: Is it true that docker compose down, without -v, keeps the data stored in named volumes?
questions.explanation: down removes the containers only. Adding -v also deletes the volumes, and with them all the data.

questions.question: How is a database service container in CI similar to Docker Compose on your PC?
questions.answer: Both start the same image with the same settings, port and healthcheck next to your code.
questions.explanation: The tests connect the same way in both places, so they behave the same locally and in CI.

questions.question: Each instruction in a Dockerfile adds one image _____.
questions.explanation: An image is a stack of layers. Docker caches them, so a rebuild only redoes the layers that changed.
